defects.rationale: All exceptions (missing file, permission errors, decode errors) are silently caught and replaced with an empty config, hiding real failures and silently running with wrong settings.

issues.observation: The review reports only one defect. A snippet containing a broad try/except around config loading almost always carries additional material defects (e.g., unvalidated/missing keys used downstream, path handling, resource leaks from unclosed file handles, insecure deserialization of config data). Stopping after the easiest issue leaves distinct defects unreported.

The rationale states the generic risk ('hiding real failures') but does not trace a concrete downstream failure path — i.e., which later operation consumes the empty config and what incorrect/unsafe behavior results. Without that, evidence alignment between line 5 and a runtime failure is weak.

revision_instructions: Re-scan the entire supplied snippet line by line and add any further material defects (correctness, security, data-integrity, resource-leak) that are visible, up to the eight-finding limit; do not add style or speculative findings.
Keep the existing line 5 swallowed_exception finding intact, but extend its rationale to name the specific downstream consumer of the empty config and the concrete incorrect behavior that results.

Verify every new finding cites the exact line containing the responsible operation, uses a taxonomy category, an integer line within range, an allowed severity, and that no two findings share the same category and line.
